text: The Court can then make an assessment as to what amount will be appropriate under the assessment, to be paid under the CFA for this lawyer.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The principles are largely similar to existing principles relating to contentious business agreements, as set out in section 115 of the Legal Profession Act.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Where a lawyer withdraws from representing a client under a CFA, existing rules under the PCR will also continue to apply.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This includes obligations on the lawyer to take reasonable care to avoid foreseeable harm to the client, such as giving reasonable notice and cooperating with the client's new lawyers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: None of these will change with the CFA.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Thomas asked about the importance of guidelines and possibly training for lawyers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will do so and we will ensure that there is sufficient guidance for the market once this is in place.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will take into account the topics highlighted by Mr Thomas.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Some of them will be addressed in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Others we can put up guidance together with Law Society, to ensure that lawyers and their clients will be aware of this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But specifically, Mr Louis Ng asked how the framework will be flexible in catering to different categories of disputes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think Mr Pillai asked how and what are the considerations we have as we consider the extensions of this framework to other types of cases.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The main tenets of the CFA framework will be set out and had been set out in the Bill, supplemented by safeguards to be prescribed under subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The categories of proceedings permitted by the CFA framework will also be set out in the subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we took this approach as we anticipated that the profile of litigants would be different for different categories of proceedings and different types of cases.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To Mr Murali Pillai's point about the principal considerations, and whether the same level of public consultation will be undertaken, the answer is yes, there will be.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The difference in terms of where we are now today on the current framework and where we may expand it to, for lawyers, obviously, when you deal with and compete on the international fora with other foreign lawyers, we want to put our lawyers on the same footing.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That may not apply in the context of domestic proceedings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For domestic proceedings, the main consideration now would be whether we can allow this so that there will be an enhancement to access to justice.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There may be more as we consult but these are the driving considerations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we will consult with key stakeholders as we look at the landscape and determine whether it would be appropriate to extend this framework to also other types of cases, to promote access to justice.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In doing so, we will study also the profile of the likely litigants who will avail themselves of any such expansion and determine in those cases whether some additional form of protection might be necessary for the framework.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And if so, we will also prescribe them.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: My Ministry is aware of the developments outlined by Mr Thomas and we will review these developments as part of a holistic study of the litigation funding landscape.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would add that After-the-Event insurance is not peculiar and not relevant only to CFAs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They are relevant across the board and generally, supplement and support the litigation funding landscape.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we will study the After-the-Event insurance in that context and look at whether or not any moves need to be made on that front.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will, at the same time, continue to monitor the impact of the various reforms, keeping our finger on the pulse of developments and lessons learnt in other jurisdictions and apply them contextually to Singapore.
